title: Full mhfe-core audit of main at aeefbdf

reviewer.name: Codex coordinator and independent protocol, release and claims reviewers

snapshot.workingTree: Earlier AUD-010 records and pre-existing audit index edits excluded from the audited Git tree and preserved. Source, tests, workflows and locks match the named commit.

extraPublicSurface: Public enum variants and fields, Default, Debug, Display and iteration
SPC Secret at the pinned integration boundary: with_capacity, locked, push, truncate, as_bytes, as_str, capacity, is_locked, is_out_of_dumps, is_out_of_children, zeroed, as_mut_bytes

SPC Isolation at the pinned integration boundary: enter, enter_with, enter_with_folders, enter_requiring, enter_requiring_process_wide, require, require_process_wide, has, outcome, measures; SecretError and native write_secret
Argon2Engine implementation, private unsafe Block cast, bare WASM checks export

coverageLedger.evidence: Phrase, Password, engine, Seed and repair ownership traced from borrowed inputs to caller-owned outputs. Experimental cryptographic scope and platform boundaries checked.

coverageLedger.logicalGroup: Secret Vault, CSP, sandbox, and transport
coverageLedger.evidence: The crate has no application vault, CSP, browser bridge or message channel.
Production crate opens no network path. Process isolation re-exports and existing handle boundary are reviewed under SEC-008 and SEC-010.

Suite 3/4 messages, geometry, masks, verifier domains, creation check and fixed points matched the pinned specification and fast transcript tests. Native Argon2 tag checked by public vectors. Random entropy is supplied by a caller.
Reviewed native stack and allocations, WASM linear memory, callback state and explicit cleanup. AUD-007-SEC002 remains open in the pinned dependency. No all-target physical residue claim.

coverageLedger.logicalGroup: Browser injection, persistence, and sensitive APIs
coverageLedger.evidence: No UI, DOM, script injection or storage. Bare WASM and its host boundary are reviewed under BLD-006.
Password limits and bounded repair widths hold. NFKD work is linear and sizing is checked, but representable allocation refusal remains AUD-006-API001.
The grants ledger covers explicit caller grants, native effects, inherited handles, Windows order and CI privileges. The historical registry listener exceeds its fixture scope.
BIP39 entropy 16–32 bytes, 12–24 words, English abbreviations, checksum, Unicode/NFKD and PBKDF2 seed behavior matched tests and pinned specification.
There is no HD master or child key derivation, address format or coin selector. The wallet check hashes the BIP39 seed.

coverageLedger.logicalGroup: BIP85, BIP38, messages, and Silent Payments
coverageLedger.evidence: No BIP85, BIP38, messaging or Silent Payments implementation.
No scripts, descriptors, multisig or Miniscript.

coverageLedger.logicalGroup: Transactions, PSBT version context, and commitments
coverageLedger.evidence: No transaction or PSBT parser, signer or commitments.

Packing, stated-length recovery, optional repair, password check and wallet check traced. The fast recorded-key corpus validates composition, and separate native Argon2 checks validate sampled tags. The ignored full-cost replay was not started.
No account discovery, network providers or balance accounting.
Exact SPC/RSC crates and bridges reviewed. Argon2Engine, callback, ownership and compile-time target boundaries audited. Upstream limitations listed independently.
Progress Breaks and late check errors traced. The synchronous API has no asynchronous or persistent state. Host callback result handling is explicitly caller-owned.

coverageLedger.logicalGroup: Public export schema and monetary fidelity
coverageLedger.evidence: No monetary export schema or CSV/JSON file writer.
Native and bare WASM canonical BIP39, profile count and erasure validation cross-checked with public vectors. WASM has no native Argon2 engine.
Workspace, root Cargo feature graph, separate fuzz and WASM packages, native-only engine, MSRV 1.99.0 and locked/toolchain builds checked.
Exact 13/13 CI with per-job runtime counts. The target matrix labels lint, link, native and emulated results individually.
Three active lockfiles and pinned archives reconciled. RustSec of unchanged inputs and retained cargo-deny evidence confirmed. Historical harness graphs reviewed as historical inputs.
This crate publishes no canonical Docker or browser distribution. Bare WASM check-module runtime is covered by BLD-006.
Package file check and publish dry run completed in exact CI. Permissions and graph checked, including separate full-cost workflow. 0.3.0 has no tag, package or attestation to verify.
No user interface or viewports in this library.
No UI navigation, inputs or state persistence.

coverageLedger.logicalGroup: Secret visibility, help, QR, and accessibility
coverageLedger.evidence: No GUI, QR output or accessibility surface. The usage example was reviewed as documentation.
Ownership boundaries among cipher, engine, profiles, protection, tests and tooling traced. Re-exported dependency APIs reviewed at the integration boundary.

coverageLedger.logicalGroup: Dead code, duplication, and false positives
coverageLedger.evidence: The copies gate found no repetitions at its 50-token threshold across source and xtask. Shared fuzz generator and shared corpus helpers were inspected.
All active fast checks passed and assert actual operation results. Stand-in key and full-cost test scopes are explicit. Prior short fuzz coverage failures and adverse origins are retained separately.

coverageLedger.logicalGroup: Workspace coding rules on the whole snapshot
coverageLedger.evidence: Actual manifests satisfy the current gate, and new tests for the three earlier forms pass. AUD-010-ARC001 remains open for other valid TOML syntax.
README rare-verifier-match outcome conflicts with recovery length rules. Known upstream limitations and the experimental status are accurately disclosed.

coverageLedger.logicalGroup: Commands, metadata, links, and legal materials
coverageLedger.evidence: Links and package membership were checked. The adjacent dependency and Rust example target different public API versions, AUD-011-DOC004.
Current exact scope and previous AUD-010 evidence separated. Historical privacy attribution remains tracked. This report adds a current finding-level follow-up register.
Coverage inputs, unchanged library code and runner claims reconciled. Native, Windows, Apple, mobile and WebAssembly limits are separately stated.
Production unsafe slice construction, test-only FFI/allocator operations and WASM export attribute reviewed. Miri reach and limitations are recorded under BLD-007.

coverageLedger.logicalGroup: Processes, IPC and the same-user attacker
coverageLedger.evidence: Native isolation tests backed by exact CI and local role outputs. Existing handles and the historical loopback registry scope are separately assessed.
Checked pointer widths, errors and target fallbacks. AUD-006-API001 remains open for the pinned Secret allocation path. Mobile runtime and other architectural gaps are explicit.

Exact native CI, Wasmtime and local debug/release runs linked and executed within the ordinary scope. Clippy evidence on other target rows is reported by actual revision. One or more required lint receipts are from the previous revision only; see the matrix.

Portable Miri and fuzz results are recorded with their scope. Production mapping path is blocked in Miri by sigfillset. Full hosted fuzz receipts, corpus replay coverage and the production Miri path remain missing. The local campaign ended with the recorded 30-second cap.

variantSearch.assessment: Compared vendored words, fixture revisions, lockfile archives and normalized Cargo output. Historical package wording remains AUD-011-DOC003.
Worked through entropy widths, loss marks, bounds and error ordering. Representable NFKD allocation remains open.

variantSearch.historicalFinding: AUD-003 memory findings, AUD-006-SEC001, AUD-007-SEC001/SEC002, AUD-008-SEC001
variantSearch.assessment: Checked payload access, caller-visible words, enums, error display, wipe-on-drop changes and callback output. RSC copy is still present. The README helper returns a Boolean.
Reviewed pre/post normalization and historical Unicode repertoire, BIP39 passphrase compatibility and pinned vectors.
Reviewed Linux PID and user namespace read-back, low lock limit outcomes, native allocation role counts and WebAssembly cleanup boundaries.
Checked the production byte comparisons, password-check index path and example boundary. The audit does not claim an all-target codegen proof.
Review covers raw input and structured branches, chronological recovery decisions, repair bounds and shared generator failure.
Reviewed target cfgs and exact runner evidence. Mobile link-only status and host-specific WebAssembly limits remain explicit.

variantSearch.assessment: Checked actual manifests, negative gate cases, supported syntax variants and all public signatures. The dependency scanner still has uncovered forms.
Compared actual profile behavior, memory policy, release configuration, artifact source, API examples and the current index. New wording/version mismatches are retained.
Checked original snapshots, file-tree identities, escaped duplicate-key limitation and executed commands. New optional fixture scope issue is independently recorded.

findings.title: Historical registry can serve files outside its synthetic fixture directory
findings.reproduction: Static control-flow review of the raw request-to-file path at the committed snapshot. No requests were sent.
findings.expected: The local fixture service can open only its explicitly served synthetic corpus files.
findings.observed: Request handling rejects parent components but does not verify that the path is relative and resolves inside the fixture directory before it reads a file.
findings.impact: On Unix, an unauthenticated same-machine client can reach the temporary listener while the optional historical harness is running and may receive files readable by its process. The library and release package do not contain the listener.
findings.evidence: The checks and resulting filesystem join in registry.rs were independently traced. The separate build harness is not affected by the same path form.
findings.recommendedFix: Serve an explicit allowlist of fixture paths from owned bytes rather than arbitrary request-mapped filesystem paths.
findings.requiredVerification: Verify ordinary Cargo fixture requests and reject non-allowlisted targets using synthetic fixtures only.

findings.title: README assigns the absence of a short reading to a verifier match
findings.reproduction: Read the wrong-password overview against the detected-length decision table and pinned specification.
findings.expected: Describe the common no-match result separately from the rare chance match.
findings.observed: The wording attaches no short reading to a chance verifier pass. Recovery returns a matching short reading and labels the verifier match. On zero matches a stated short length is refused, and an unstated length can yield an unverified 24-word reading.
findings.impact: A reader could misunderstand what a verifier match or a surviving short reading means when recovering a backup. Runtime code and its detailed docs agree with the specification.
findings.evidence: Three reviewers independently compared the README, source and recovery rules. The suite tests exercise both branches.
findings.recommendedFix: Separate the zero-match and rare-match cases and retain the distinction between a verifier match and wallet identification.
findings.requiredVerification: Cross-check wording against the match, no-match, different-length and ambiguous recovery cases.

findings.title: Historical public audit records retain private decision attribution
findings.reproduction: Inspect the historical narrative, JSON and index against Report privacy in the workspace audit rules.
findings.expected: Record technical decisions, evidence and dispositions without attributing them to a person or private conversation.
findings.observed: The tracked documents attribute technical acceptances and internal decisions to a requester and refer to private conversations. Their details are not repeated here.
findings.impact: The current public record retains unnecessary personal attribution. The technical decisions, findings and evidence can remain intact when that attribution is removed.
findings.evidence: The index and the Markdown and JSON record were compared with the current explicit privacy rule.
findings.recommendedFix: Apply authorized privacy redaction that preserves the original technical conclusions, evidence and dispositions.
findings.requiredVerification: Verify both report formats and the index for attribution and confirm preserved technical evidence.

findings.title: Historical package checker overstates its commit-blob comparison
findings.reproduction: Compare promised blob coverage with the generated-file branches of blobs_match.
findings.expected: Distinguish archived byte equality and generated-file membership from comparison to source Git blobs.
findings.observed: The guide and success text say every packaged file equals its commit blob. The normalized Cargo.toml and Cargo VCS metadata are skipped by this comparison. The separate archive comparison covers their bytes.
findings.impact: Readers can infer that generated metadata was validated against the source commit by a check that only compares other files. The historical byte-reproducibility result remains separate.
findings.evidence: Static inspection of the stated contract, loop and status output.
findings.recommendedFix: Qualify the old check as blob equality for tracked source material and list the generated-file exceptions.
findings.requiredVerification: Reconcile documented checks, file membership and output with the exact comparison branches.

findings.title: README dependency and neighboring example use different APIs
findings.reproduction: Compare the adjacent dependency snippet and Rust example with the API at v0.2.0 and the current manifest.
findings.expected: The example compiles for its stated version, or the documentation explicitly pairs the example with its intended unreleased version.
findings.observed: The dependency snippet selects 0.2. In v0.2.0 (d203948833d16399a163a89db546b92448c5b212), encrypt and decrypt return Phrase and Recovery after the Result is unwrapped. The README matches ControlFlow::Continue as in unreleased 0.3.0.
findings.impact: Copying the dependency and example together yields a Rust type error at both matches. No defect in either library version follows from the mixed instructions.
findings.evidence: Exact tagged public signatures and current signatures were read independently. The release tag and package identity were verified by the release review.
findings.recommendedFix: Use an example for 0.2 or label the unreleased 0.3 API example with the dependency source that provides it.
findings.requiredVerification: Compile the presented example with the exact dependency described immediately above it.

informationalNotes: AUD-004-ARC001 already records the narrow historical verification contracts. verify2 uses mtimes and untracked paths, so a deleted tracked path is not checked. Its diff digest is only printed. The old JSON checker compares raw key spelling, so escape-equivalent keys are outside its check. Neither limitation establishes that an old recorded verdict was wrong. The current report uses the complete tracked inventory and decoded-key validation.

AUD-010 is retained as the uncommitted review of 00c070c. Its command outputs were checked separately from its prose. The cited semver tool skipped all 260 checks on the version transition. Its Miri harness models an aligned cast and does not execute the production WorkArea path. Its code generation log records compilation. These results are not stronger evidence of semantic compatibility or optimizer behavior.

password_check::Check and repair::Change return words deliberately requested by their callers. The output ownership boundary in SECURITY.md applies to those values. No extra hidden payload leak was established by this review.
Only the optional historical registry uses the affected listener. Its sibling build harness strips all leading Unix separators, so the same absolute-path issue does not apply there.

The specification test submodule is a pinned input. Relevant protocol text, manifests and public vectors are reconciled at the gitlink. The rest of that separate repository is not a second audit scope.

remediation.evidence: Local repair arrays and protection storage are explicitly wiped. Native and bare-WASM tests pass, with the separate RSC copy retained as AUD-007-SEC002.
The size refusal and documentation hold. Representable allocation refusal still terminates in SPC 0.2.0.
The active graphs have aligned security dependencies and the three RustSec scopes were checked against identical lockfiles.
Isolation uses the first PID and user namespace distinction. The actual role checks pass on native Linux and CI.
Code-rules reviews fuzz Rust while excluding generated builds/corpora. The exact gate and unit tests pass.
Recovery and passphrase entries exist, and their input and outcome assertions were read.
Android and iOS device lint/link passed, but device/emulator runtime and the simulator remain uncovered.
SECURITY describes observable memory and timing settings.
32651c2 added the index and contents list. bd41e4d completed the two-column table. The README distinguishes local checks from hosted CI.
Current README and coverage report attribute their figures to 1fe8761.
Current AGENTS references the matrix, fuzzing and release workflow correctly.
SECURITY describes separate read-only package, attestation, and draft-job grants.
Changelog separates library and repository changes.
SECURITY reports up to 144 KiB on measured Linux x86-64 and qualifies unmeasured systems.
Word indices for checks use protected Secret storage and check_word borrows the array. Native fast tests and bare-WASM check-word vectors passed.
RSC 0.2.0 lane tail still owns a Copy value with no explicit wipe. No physical residue claim across targets.

ctutils comparison now replaces hand-built early termination prevention. Fresh functional tests passed. Older helper exploration is a separate configuration and this audit does not re-establish every optimized comparison path.
Bare Wasm 28/28 in exact CI, with separately recorded WASI and browser gaps.
Recovery fuzzer checks rejected counts, verifier mismatch, ordering and original short length inclusion.
Structured password-check fuzz cases assert success, erasure and mismatch candidates, plus pinned vectors.
Shared phrase_of generator centralizes admitted sizes and refuses silent valid-input construction failure.
Public API gate parses continued attributes and rejects unsupported forms. Exact host result lists 22 items and its gate tests passed.
Mandatory vendored row and digest, no silent empty directory acceptance. Gate and refusal tests passed.
All six targets and the bare-WASM runner appear in TARGETS.md.
Documentation example checks the required outcome before host secret input.
Statistical checks and wallet identification clarified in API/security text. A subsequent README edit introduces the narrower wording regression AUD-011-DOC001.
Seed::derive documents the older Unicode compatibility boundary.
Packaged README references unavailable files by project URL. Exact package job passed.
README contains index and primary guide links, two-column contents and audit history.
Audit record distinguishes the measured source from later documentation. Latest measurements are labeled separately.

ed770a1 removed plaintext printing and bd41e4d completed exact-length selection. The README helper accepts typed Phrase and Password references and returns only a Boolean, with host duties in the separate rustdoc example.
WASM graph and three RustSec steps checked; exact dependency inputs unchanged after the passing RustSec run.
A constructor error on valid-length synthetic entropy terminates the fuzz run instead of skipping the case.
Unit tests assert allocator protection according to policy rather than assuming all pages are locked. Exact host debug, release and CI tests pass.
AGENTS and audit.yml describe three lockfiles.
Wasm stack and process end wording distinguishes instance lifetime and physical wiping, and states possible overflow effects.

The three originally tested forms are handled and their regression test passed. Valid TOML literal-string versions, quoted dependency keys and braces inside comments still evade the simplified parser. This is the same gate defect class. Current manifests comply.
Repair scratch commentary now distinguishes local fixed arrays, native clearing, and the documented 0.2.0 upstream copy. Read together with SECURITY.md target limits.

limitations: Ordinary audit of mhfe_core. No full-cost Argon2 vector replay, publish action, tagged package or attestation verification for 0.3.0. The full-cost test remained ignored by the fast suites.

Miri reaches nine syscall-free tests in each retained aliasing run. Native Secret construction hits unsupported libc::sigfillset. The isolated cast model cannot establish the production allocator path. No all-target timing or complete memory-residue proof.
The mobile rows are compilation evidence only, and the iOS simulator has no native execution. Bare WebAssembly runs in Wasmtime. A browser application, its CSP and its engine are separate scopes.
Upstream protection and Reed–Solomon code were reviewed at the exact pinned integration boundaries. Pinned dependency hashes and tests are not a complete audit of those repositories.
The 28 historical harness lockfiles received source/cache integrity review where archives existed. Fresh RustSec coverage is scoped to the three active unchanged lockfiles.

Historical harness source was reviewed, preserving its original evidence and inputs. Historical probes that use obsolete checkouts, external processes, credentials, or mutable caches were not started.

The 96.84 percent coverage is retained from the documented 1fe8761 measurement. Its log and row totals were reconciled, and the final commit changes documentation only. The run does not have an independent contemporaneous input hash.

The exact CI does not execute a RustSec workflow because dependencies did not change. All three active manifests, locks and the audit workflow are byte-identical to the passing RustSec snapshot. Neither that result nor archive hashes exclude future advisories.
Report status reflects confirmed defects in required checks. The new findings are Low and non-blocking individually, and none demonstrates a break in production encryption or recovery.

Three five-minute attempts completed before the local limit changed. Recovery was interrupted and contributes only its last observed counter. Repair and password_check ran with a hard 30-second process cap. Missing hosted extended fuzz, corpus minimization and coverage remain explicit gaps.

grants.purpose: Supply Argon2 and observe or cancel operations
grants.admits: The caller engine receives protocol password and salt bytes. The unchecked-container callback sees a candidate before its creation check.
grants.narrowestForm: Narrow borrowed slices and explicit callback scopes
grants.whyNoNarrower: The host owns the engine and must withhold candidate output until the check returns Continue.
grants.order: Admit → forward rounds → unchecked callback → independent recovery check → return.

grants.purpose: Retain and wipe buffers, minimize temporary native stack residue
grants.admits: Lock and exclusion can be refused. Existing host snapshots and WebAssembly residue lie outside the clearing range.
grants.narrowestForm: Precise buffers and native best-effort overwrite
grants.whyNoNarrower: Keep bounded payload ownership, report lock/exclusion and preserve caller responsibility.
grants.order: Normalize into exact Secret; clear stack after the body.

grants.purpose: Native Argon2id aligned contiguous working memory
grants.admits: Alignment and lifetime rely on the pinned allocator. Host-sized WorkArea can exhaust memory.
grants.narrowestForm: One slice cast inside a small helper
grants.whyNoNarrower: The typed view and original allocation are never aliased.
grants.order: Allocate → borrow for engine → wipe on normal return/refusal.

grants.purpose: Constrain external reading, process effects and later handle acquisition
grants.admits: Inherited descriptors, unprivileged namespace availability and system read-back limit guarantees. Existing processes and threads are outside a current-thread-only application.
grants.narrowestForm: Enter before secrets and thread creation, inspect outcomes and close unneeded handles
grants.whyNoNarrower: The crate keeps initialization and host permissions under caller ownership.
grants.order: On Linux call before the first Secret and engine threads. Constrain namespaces, read-back and restrictions before the secret work.

grants.grant: Windows DACL, restricted job and low integrity
grants.purpose: Restrict peer process/thread access and child/UI effects
grants.admits: Pre-existing handles and privileged peers remain relevant. Low-labelled directories are still writable. Windows can hide threads in the post-lowering census.
grants.narrowestForm: Apply DACL and defaults before lowering integrity, then require relevant confirmed outcomes
grants.whyNoNarrower: Existing handles cannot be revoked reliably by the application, and no-network requires a suitable container token.
grants.order: WER and mitigations → job → open token → process and default DACL → thread census and DACL → low integrity → evidence and post-lowering census. Isolation is not atomic during startup.

grants.purpose: Run profiles in a portable engine
grants.admits: The instance and the engine owner can observe memory. No protected-stack or native isolation grant.
grants.narrowestForm: Caller-owned engine with explicit data flow
grants.whyNoNarrower: The test export has no input pointer or FFI memory access.
grants.order: Build publicly pinned vector module → invoke checks → count 28.

grants.grant: GitHub contents read and runner install authority
grants.purpose: Check out code and install pinned toolchains and tools
grants.admits: Build scripts and compiler plugins run on the runner. MinGW installation uses sudo on a disposable runner.
grants.narrowestForm: Read-only workflow token and credentials not persisted
grants.whyNoNarrower: The CI build requires dependencies and host linker tools.
grants.order: Checkout → verify tools → checks/package → transfer artifacts.

grants.purpose: Bind package bytes to trusted workflow
grants.admits: The job can attest another subject if its inputs are substituted.
grants.narrowestForm: Separate job scopes and named package artifact
grants.whyNoNarrower: Write permission used by the attestation action only.
grants.order: Build and fuzz prerequisite → package → attest.

grants.admits: A token of this scope can also change other repository contents.
grants.narrowestForm: Separate draft job with no project execution
grants.whyNoNarrower: GitHub has no narrower token scope for the release creation call.
grants.order: Attest → download package/notes → draft. Full-cost vectors are a separate publication condition.

grants.purpose: Provide Cargo a synthetic sparse registry
grants.admits: Clients in the same machine can reach the service, currently outside the intended fixture scope.
grants.narrowestForm: Serve an allowlist of in-memory synthetic fixture bytes
grants.whyNoNarrower: No arbitrary filesystem access is necessary to test Cargo caching.
grants.order: Listener starts before Cargo requests and ends with the harness process.
